blocks.text:
Michael Martin
Chief Operating Officer
Coleman Ltd
Dear Michael,

Thank you for entrusting this search to us. It means a great deal that you have asked Northgate to find the person who will lead your engineering organization, and we do not take the responsibility lightly. A leadership hire of this kind sets the direction of a function for years, and we treat it that way. This letter sets out what we have agreed, so that both of us can point to the same page later if a question ever comes up. I have tried to keep the language plain, even where the letter turns to terms. Nothing here should surprise you; it is simply our understanding, written down, and I am happy to talk through any line of it before you sign.
The assignment

You have engaged us, on a retained basis, to identify and recommend a Vice President of Engineering for {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}. We understand the seat to be a senior operating role, reporting into your leadership team, with responsibility for the engineering function and the people in it. The written brief we build together at kickoff will govern the search, and we will hold ourselves to it rather than to a generic profile. If your sense of the role changes as we go, we will change the brief with you.
How we will work

A retained search runs in stages, and we will keep you close at each of them. We begin by mapping the market and agreeing a written specification for the role. From there we build a long list, approach the strongest names discreetly, and narrow to a slate we are willing to stand behind. You will meet that slate, we will manage the interviews and the scheduling around them, and we will complete thorough references before anyone receives an offer. Throughout, we describe candidates by their current role rather than by name in anything that circulates, and we ask you to do the same on your side. A careless word can end a good conversation, so the discretion is not a formality; it is how the work gets done.
The people on your search

You will work with a small team. James Grant, our Senior Consultant, will lead the assessment of the senior candidates and bring his judgment to the shortlist. Jeffrey Patterson, our Research Consultant, will keep the search moving day to day and be your point of contact for scheduling and follow-up. John Chang, our Research Associate, will map the market and build the long list the consultants work from. I will stay close to the assignment myself and remain reachable to you at any point. If the chemistry with any of us is not right, tell me, and I will fix it.
Fee and start

Our fee for the assignment is {{fact:f:E-2016-001.fee}}, and the engagement commences on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}}. The fee is a fixed professional fee for the search, not a percentage that moves with the eventual compensation, so you know the cost of the work at the outset and we have no incentive to steer you toward a more expensive hire.
Fees and payment

We invoice the fee in three parts across the life of the search. The first third falls due on commencement, the second on presentation of the agreed slate, and the final third on the successful candidate's acceptance of your offer. Reasonable out-of-pocket costs, such as travel we agree in advance, are billed at cost and itemized. Invoices are payable within thirty days of receipt.
Term, and how either of us may end it

The engagement continues until the role is filled or until either of us chooses to end it. If you decide to withdraw the assignment, the fee earned to that point remains payable and any portion not yet earned is not. If we find ourselves unable to serve you well, we will tell you plainly and part on fair terms. Neither of us should feel bound to a search that has stopped working, and in our experience saying so early is a kindness to both sides.
Confidentiality

Discretion is the heart of this work. We treat your search, your reasons for it, and the identities of the people we approach as confidential, and we expect the same care from you. Candidates who speak with us have not, as a rule, spoken to their current employers, and their trust is ours to protect. For that reason we write about candidates by their seat rather than their name until an offer is in hand, and we keep the circle of people who know the details as small as the work allows.
What we will need from you

A search moves at the speed of its client as much as its consultant. We will ask for prompt feedback after each round of interviews, for a single point of contact on your side so that messages do not cross, and for candor about how your thinking evolves. If your view of the role shifts as you meet people, tell us early and we will adjust the brief with you. The one thing that slows a search is silence, and we will do our part to make sure it never comes from ours.
Limitation of liability

We will bring real care and experience to the assignment, but we do not guarantee a hire, and our responsibility to you is limited to the fee paid for the search. We are not liable for indirect or consequential losses. Once we have done our work and presented our slate, the hiring decision rests with you, as it should.
Governing law

This letter is governed by the law of the state in which our office sits, and any dispute under it will be resolved there. We would much prefer to settle any disagreement in conversation, and over many years we almost always have.

If this reflects our understanding, please countersign below and return one copy to Jeffrey, who will open the file and confirm your kickoff session. We are glad to be working with you on this, Michael, and we are ready to begin. The one thing we need from you now is your countersignature.

To: James Grant, John Chang
From: Jeffrey Patterson
Re: Kickoff — Vice President of Engineering search for Coleman Ltd

Our goal for this search is simple to state: to place a Vice President of Engineering that {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} is glad to have hired a year from now. Everything below serves that end, and I have kept the memo short so it is easy to hold in mind. The engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}}, and this note sets out how we will run the early weeks so that we start clean and stay aligned. Our client sponsor is Michael Martin, and he has asked to be the single point of contact on Coleman's side, which keeps our reporting simple and our messages from crossing.

A word before the work. We do not yet know this organization as well as we will, and the kickoff conversation is where that starts. Michael Martin has offered us his time early, and we should use it to understand the shape of the team the new leader will inherit and the decisions waiting for them. Hold your questions for that session rather than assuming; the brief is only ever as good as what we learn there.
The early work

items: Market map. John Chang will chart the engineering-leadership market and identify the pools worth working, reaching into adjacent sectors where the relevant experience also sits.
Specification. James Grant and I will turn the kickoff conversation into a written brief we can hold the search to, and circulate it for the client's sign-off before we approach anyone.
Sourcing. Once the map and the brief are set, we begin discreet approaches, describing the role rather than naming the people we speak with.
Confidentiality. We write about candidates by their current seat, not their name, in anything that leaves the room, and we will ask the client to do the same.
Cadence. We will hold a short internal review each week and send the client a written update on a steady rhythm, so no one has to ask where things stand.

blocks.text: None of these steps is complicated on its own. What makes a search succeed is doing them in order and not skipping ahead: a map before a list, a list before an approach, an approach before a slate. If we hold that discipline, and keep Michael Martin informed as we go, the rest tends to take care of itself.
This week

Before anything else, John Chang will circulate a first cut of the market map for James Grant and me to react to. I will confirm the kickoff notes with Michael Martin and lock the specification review for early next week. A good brief for this role names the two or three outcomes the new leader has to deliver in the first year, not a wish list of traits; keep that test in mind as you shape it. If either of you sees a gap in the brief as it stands, raise it now. Correcting the brief is cheap while it is still on paper, and I would like us to open the approaches with it fully settled.
The single thing that has to happen first is the market map. Everything we do after it depends on it, so let us get a first version in front of ourselves by Friday and build from there.
Dear Michael,

Good progress to report, and one small thing I would ask of you. Since the search opened, John Chang has built out the market map for the Vice President of Engineering role at {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}, and James Grant has begun reading the strongest sitting engineering leaders against the specification we agreed. We are describing candidates by their current seat rather than by name at this stage, as we always do while a search is live, and I would ask that Coleman Ltd hold to the same discretion on your side.

The ask is a modest one. So that nothing about this search travels wider than it must, we would like to route every candidate document to you alone, Michael Martin, as the client's single point of contact. If you would rather a second name be copied, tell me and we will set it up straight away.

I will keep this thread moving from our side. As ever, I am your day-to-day contact — Jeffrey Patterson — with James Grant on the senior assessment and John Chang on the research bench. If anything at all is unclear, a short call is easier than a long note, and I am glad to pick up the phone.
Sincerely,
Vice President of Engineering — Retained Search

blocks.text: Working Session Minutes — Vice President of Engineering Search

These minutes record the working session held with our client to review progress on the Vice President of Engineering search for {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}. The purpose of the session was to assess the developing long list and to plan the first round of client interviews. The notes below are a summary. Where a decision was reached, it is marked as such; where a matter was left open, that is noted too.
Present

items: John Chang, Research Associate
Jeffrey Patterson, Research Consultant
James Grant, Senior Consultant
Michael Martin, Chief Operating Officer, Coleman Ltd

blocks.text: Where the search stands

John Chang presented the market map and the long list built from it. The list is deliberately broad at this stage, and it will narrow as the approaches return. James Grant observed that the quality of the pool is consistent with the specification, though he cautioned that two of the most attractive names may prove difficult to move.

Consistent with the firm's practice, candidates were discussed by their current role rather than by name. The group considered, in particular, an engineering lead at a regional logistics group and a divisional head of engineering at a listed software company. Both were judged worth a discreet approach. No commitment was made on either, and neither has been contacted as of this session.

There was a short discussion of coverage. James Grant asked whether the map had reached far enough into the software sector, and John Chang undertook to extend it into two adjacent fields before the next review. It was agreed that a wider map was worth the additional time it would take, and that the list should not be closed prematurely. The group recorded no concern about the pace of the work to date.
The client interviews

Michael Martin set out how he would like the first round to run. He asked that interviews be kept to a small panel on his side, and that scheduling flow through Jeffrey Patterson to avoid crossed wires. He was measured about timing, and asked that we not compress the process at the expense of thorough references.

It was agreed that a first slate would not be presented until the current approaches have run their course. James Grant will judge readiness rather than commit to a fixed date. This qualification matters, in the group's view: the field is still widening, and a premature slate would serve no one. The point was recorded so that it is not revisited without cause.
Action items

rows: Extend the market map into the two adjacent sectors raised in the session and refresh the long list.
Frame the approach to the two priority candidates and judge when a slate is ready to present.
Coordinate first-round interview scheduling with Michael Martin and hold provisional dates.
Confirm the interview panel on the client side and the compensation band with the board.

Status Report — Vice President of Engineering Search
Prepared for the leadership of Coleman Ltd by Jeffrey Patterson, Research Consultant. This report covers the period since our last update and marks roughly the midpoint of the engagement.
Where we stand

The short version is that the search is on track. We have moved from mapping the market to working a live field of candidates, and we expect to bring you a first slate in the coming weeks. Nothing has arisen that changes our confidence in filling the role for {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} well and on a sensible timeline. The rest of this report fills in that picture.
What we have accomplished

John Chang has completed the market map and built it into a long list that we are now actively working. The map reached wider than we first planned, into two adjacent sectors where the relevant leadership experience also sits, and that breadth has paid off in the quality of the names we are speaking with.

James Grant has led the assessment of the strongest candidates against the specification. He has held first exploratory conversations with several of them, all conducted discreetly and, as always, with candidates described by their current role rather than by name in anything we circulate. Those conversations have told us as much about who to pursue harder as about who to set aside.

For my part, I have kept the threads moving and the scheduling clean, which at this stage is most of the work. A search of this kind lives or dies on follow-up, and no candidate we care about has been left waiting on us for an answer.

One useful outcome of the early conversations is that they have tested the specification against real people. The brief has held up well. Nothing we have heard has sent us back to redraw the role, which tells us the kickoff work was sound and that the field we are building is the right one to be building. Where a candidate has fallen short, it has been on a clear line in the brief rather than on a vague sense of fit.
The budget

The engagement remains within its agreed terms. Our fixed professional fee of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.fee}} covers the search through to placement, and we do not foresee any additional cost beyond the modest, pre-agreed out-of-pocket items. You should expect no surprises on the invoice, and we will flag anything unusual well before it reaches one.
What comes next

Over the next several weeks we will bring the current approaches to a close and narrow the long list to a shortlist we are prepared to stand behind. We will then complete a first round of references on the leading candidates before presenting a slate, so that when you meet them you are meeting people we have already checked. We will hold to our regular rhythm of updates throughout, and I will confirm the date of the slate presentation as soon as it is firm.

When the slate is ready, we will present each candidate with a written summary and our own read on strengths and risks, still by current role until you have decided to proceed. We will suggest an interview order and handle the scheduling from our side. All we will ask of you at that point is a small, consistent panel and prompt feedback after each conversation, since a slate goes stale quickly if it is left to sit.
What we are watching

Two risks deserve mention, neither of them pressing. The first is availability: one or two of the most attractive candidates sit in roles they are not obviously looking to leave, and moving them will take patience. The second is notice periods, which can add time at the end of a search that looks fast in the middle. We are managing both by keeping the field wider than we strictly need until the shortlist is firm.

There is also the constant of confidentiality. The people we are speaking with have not, as a rule, told their current employers, and we protect that carefully. It is the reason we ask that Coleman Ltd hold the same discretion on candidate identities that we do. So far the process has stayed tight, and we intend to keep it that way.

In short, the search is where it should be at the halfway mark, and the next milestone is the shortlist. James Grant and John Chang will bring the field to that point over the coming weeks, and I will keep you posted the moment there is something firm to share.
